question.text: Consider an imaginary ion <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi><none/><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>-</mo></mrow><mprescripts/><mn>22</mn><mn>48</mn></mmultiscripts></math>. The nucleus contains '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></math>'<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>%</mo></math> more neutrons than the number of electrons in the ion. The value of '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></math>' is

solution.text:
X22483-

In an atomic representation XZA

Z is atomic number = 22

A is atomic mass number = 48.

No. of protons  = Z = 22

No. of neutrons =A-Z = 48-22 = 26

No. of electrons =P-charge = 22+3 = 25

% of extra neutrons than electrons =26-2525×100=4 % = a%

So, the value of a=4.
